summary: A compact, actor-playable bereavement beat with a clear progression: dreaded arrival, Sayed’s last words, the child’s direct question, then Fatma’s controlled invitation. The letter is period-plausible and emotionally effective, provided the final phrases are delivered without patriotic grandeur.
scene_issues: The march cue may overstate the patriotic note immediately after an intimate loss; keep it restrained until the transition into the next beat.

performance.delivery: Mostafa remains upright and offers the letter directly to Fatma because he promised Sayed. Let the pause after «سَيِّدْ» catch slightly, but do not openly break down.

lines.speaker: SAYED
issues: «وِرَبِّيهْ رَاجِلْ» and «مِشْ نَدْمَانْ» approach familiar patriotic-death phrasing, so the performance must keep them personal rather than slogan-like.

performance.delivery: Read it as words Sayed wrote practically before danger, not as a ghost speaking from beyond death. Stay plain and intimate, allowing only «وِأَنَا مِشْ نَدْمَانْ» to carry a quiet final release.

lines.text: «فَاطْمَةْ… لَوْ الْجَوَابْ دَهْ وِصِلِّكْ مِنْ إِيدْ غِيرْ إِيدِي، يِبْقَى خَلَاصْ. مَا تِعَيَّطِيشْ قُدَّامْ عَلِي. قُولِيلُهْ أَبُوهْ رَاحْ عَشَانْ نِرْجَعْ السُّوِيسْ… وِرَبِّيهْ رَاجِلْ. وِأَنَا مِشْ نَدْمَانْ.»

performance.delivery: Ali looks directly at Mostafa and asks the literal question he needs answered. Keep it small and unperformed, with no adult understanding added to the child’s voice.

lines.speaker: MOSTAFA
issues: The reassurance is natural but familiar and only lightly individualized to Mostafa.

performance.delivery: At the boy’s height, Mostafa gives him one firm truth and one kindness. Hold Ali’s gaze and resist smiling or sounding falsely cheerful.

lines.text: كُنْتْ مَعَاهْ. وِكَانْ بِيِحْكِي عَنَّكْ عَلَى طُولْ.

performance.delivery: Fatma steps aside and addresses Mostafa almost maternally, accepting both him and what he has brought. Keep the words steady; the effort not to cry should register only in the breath.
